about.text: Glue made from casein mixed with water, hydrated lime and often caustic soda; with enough lime it resists water. Used in crude form for woodwork since the Middle Ages, made as an industry from the 19th century, and in wide demand for military aircraft from 1916–17.

how.text: The lime does the work: it dissolves the casein into a glue and, as it reacts, makes the dried film resist water. Adjusting the balance of sodium hydroxide and lime trades water resistance against pot life. Alkali dissolves the casein, so no cooking is needed.

steps.name: soak
steps.note: 100 parts of casein, ground to pass a 20-mesh sieve, are soaked in 150 parts of water.
Sodium hydroxide, 11 parts in 50 parts of water.
Hydrated lime, 20 parts in 50 parts of water.
